pageCache.pageTitle: Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND) - Morelands Primary School - Be the best that we can be
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND)
Welcome to our unique school with more than 300 pupils in the mainstream part of the school and not just one but two resourced provisions of 24 pupils. We have a much larger than average number of children who receive additional support for special educational needs.
To ensure all children receive their entitlements we have a team of talented, skilled and dedicated adults: Mrs Harvey, who is our Mainstream Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator and Mrs Chapman, who is the Teacher in Charge of Resourced Provisions.
There are three other teachers who work within the resourced provisions who are highly skilled in ensuring provision for children with Speech, Language and Communication needs. Admissions for these provisions is through the county special educational needs process.
We have a fantastic team of learning support assistants who work with children in need of additional support under the guidance of the class teachers, Teacher in Charge, and SENCO.
The world of special educational needs can be very confusing. The staff at Morelands are pleased to be able to help. Please do contact us if you need to.
For children living more than 3 miles away, you may be entitled to transport. To apply please see; http://www3.hants.gov.uk/traveltoschool/sch-transport/stforms.htm

pageCache.pageTitle: School Clubs - Morelands Primary School - Be the best that we can be
pageCache.text:
School Clubs
At our school, we believe that learning doesn’t stop at the classroom door. Our wide range of clubs gives pupils the chance to explore new interests, develop their talents, and enjoy spending time with friends in a fun and supportive environment.
We offer a variety of exciting clubs that run on a half‑termly rotation, giving pupils the opportunity to try something new throughout the year. Popular clubs include Football, Badminton, Art, Lego, and Spanish, with fresh options introduced regularly.
Whether children want to get active, be creative, build amazing things, or learn a new language, there’s something for everyone. Our clubs help pupils grow in confidence, develop teamwork skills, and discover new passions.
We look forward to seeing pupils get involved and explore what inspires them!

pageCache.pageTitle: Attendance - Morelands Primary School - Be the best that we can be
pageCache.text:
Attendance
At Morelands we are committed to working in partnership with parents and carers to give children the very best education and life chances.
Miss Poscotis
Mrs McGuinness
Mrs Appleford
Mr Bilbe
Did you know…
Should I keep my child at home
If your child is absent from school, you must notify the school office on the first day of absence.
If school has a medical concern, the office will ring to discuss this and if it is felt that the child is too poorly to remain in school, they will need to be collected, with siblings remaining until the end of the school day.
Do I need to keep my child off school? (English and translations) | HSC Public Health Agency Click the link
Absences
Authorised – is when the school agrees with the reason for absence.
Unauthorised – no acceptable reason is given for absence.
Examples of absences which the school is unlikely to authorise can include:
Children have 13 weeks annual holiday from school. Parents/carers are expected to take holidays at this time. Education law states that parents do not have a right to take their child out of school for a holiday during term time. Only in exceptional circumstances may a headteacher grant permission for leave during term time.
Inadequate clothing for school
Child being used as a carer
Problems with transport
Mild illness (as stated)
Lateness
Non-urgent medical treatment
External club activity
School refusal or truancy
Birthdays
Shopping trips
Holidays
Lateness for school
School gates open at 8.35am and registers are closed at 8.45am
If a pupil arrives after this time, it is recorded as an unauthorised absence. Contact the school in the first instance if you are concerned about this. If a child is frequently late, the parents may be failing to ensure that their child is receiving full time education and could be prosecuted by the Local Authority. Within the Children’s Services Department, the Education Welfare Service is responsible for matters of attendance and truancy.
Attendance at Morelands is good. However, if a child is frequently late, parents may be failing to ensure that their child is receiving full time education and could be referred to the Education Welfare Service who are responsible for matters of attendance and truancy.
We all want good outcomes for your children and working together is the best way to achieve this. If you are finding things challenging, please reach out and speak with a member of staff on the Attendance Team. Miss P, Mrs Appleford or Mrs McGuinness are always here to help.

pageCache.pageTitle: Uniform - Morelands Primary School - Be the best that we can be
pageCache.text:
Uniform
Please make sure all items are named including coats and clothes worn on non-uniform day.
Boys:
Navy/black/grey trousers or shorts (not sportswear)
White shirt/polo shirt
Navy jumper/Sweatshirt/Cardigan
White/grey/black socks
Girls:
School sweatshirts, cardigans and reversible showerproof fleeces are available from the School Office. These bear the school badge which was designed by a pupil. PE “T” shirts, sun hats and school bags are also available from the office. Second-hand uniform is available on request – 50 pence an item.
As a Healthy School, we promote ‘sun safety’ so all garments must cover children’s shoulders. Children are encouraged to use their own named sun cream and sunblock in summer and lip salve in winter.
NOTE: Children must be able to apply these products themselves, as staff do not assist.
Blue and white gingham dresses
White blouse/polo shirt
Navy jumper/Sweatshirt/Cardigan
Suitable black/navy closed toe school shoes
White/grey/black socks or tights
PE Kit
All children will require a separate PE kit consisting of the following:
Children must not wear earrings during PE lessons. If your child is unable to take their earrings out by themselves please make sure they are taken out at home on PE days.
All items of clothing must be clearly marked with the child’s name. Any item of clothing which is named will be returned to the child if found, but any unnamed items will be put in “Lost Property”.

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest Schools - Morelands Primary School - Be the best that we can be
pageCache.text:
Forest Schools
Living our values through outdoor learning
At Morelands Primary School, Forest School plays an important role in supporting our vision for happy, confident children who enjoy learning and achieve their best.
Forest School gives our pupils regular opportunities to learn outdoors, connect with nature and develop key life skills that reflect our school values.
Forest School and our School Values
Forest School supports our vision by encouraging children to:
Children are encouraged to explore, ask questions and learn through first‑hand experience. Forest School helps to develop curiosity, creativity and a love of learning that links closely to classroom learning.
Be confident and resilient
Outdoor learning allows children to try new things, face challenges and persevere. Forest School supports children to build resilience, independence and belief in themselves.
Show respect and care
Children learn to respect one another, listen to different ideas and work as part of a team. They also develop respect for the natural environment and understand the importance of caring for the world around them.
Be kind and inclusive
Forest School provides a calm, supportive environment where children can succeed at their own pace. It encourages kindness, cooperation and positive relationships, helping every child feel included and valued.
What is Forest School?
Forest School is a child‑centred approach to learning that takes place outdoors. Children learn through play, exploration and practical activities, building skills that support their personal, social and emotional development as well as their learning in the classroom.
Sessions are carefully planned to be purposeful, engaging and enjoyable.
What do children do at Forest School?
Activities change with the seasons and the interests of the children, and may include:
Children are encouraged to take safe risks, make choices and learn from experience, while being supported by staff throughout.
Exploring nature and observing wildlife
Building dens and shelters
Creating artwork using natural materials
Playing games and completing challenges together
Using imagination through storytelling and play
Who takes part?
Forest School is enjoyed by children from Reception to Year 6. Activities are adapted to suit different ages and abilities, allowing children to build skills and confidence over time.
Safety and wellbeing
Children’s safety and wellbeing are always our priority.
Forest School supports children to understand and manage risk safely, helping them to become responsible and confident learners.
Activities are carefully planned and risk‑assessed
Children are supervised at all times
What should children wear?
Forest School takes place in most weather conditions, so children should wear:
Parents will be informed about suitable clothing in advance of sessions.
Comfortable, weather‑appropriate clothing
Layers that can get muddy
Sturdy footwear
Forest School at Morelands
Forest School reflects our commitment to providing a rich, nurturing and inclusive curriculum, where children feel safe to explore, grow and succeed.
It supports our vision of developing confident, caring and resilient learners who are well prepared for the next stage of their education and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Premium - Morelands Primary School - Be the best that we can be
pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
What is Pupil Premium?
The Pupil Premium Grant was introduced by the Department for Education (DfE) in 2011, as additional funding for pupils; who receive Free School Meals (FSM), who are Looked After Children (LAC) and those who are from Service Families. This is because the DfE has recognised that a good education is the key to improving young people’s life chances. Pupil Premium provides additional funding specifically linked to the objective of boosting pupils’ attainment.
Pupil Premium is additional funding for publicly funded schools in England to raise the attainment of disadvantaged pupils of all abilities and to close the gaps between them and their peers.
All schools receive the following funding for each child registered as eligible for free school meals at any point in the last 6 years:
If you are in receipt of any of the following, Morelands Primary School may be eligible for the grant. Please come in to the School Office, where Mrs McGuinness, Ms Wooding or Miss Poscotis, will happily help or check your entitlement by using the following link https://www.cloudforedu.org.uk/ofsm/hants/
Information is always treated in the strictest confidence.
Any additional funding will enable us to provide more for the children at school. You only need to apply once as Pupil Premium funding lasts for 6 years.
